title: Field-fibre criterion for universal degree-zero structure-sheaf pushforward
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $f$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Here proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation also requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. For every field $k$ [def-weil-field] and every morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $X_u=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$ (the sheaf fibre product), and assume that the canonical structure map $k\to\Gamma(X_u,\mathcal O_{X_u})$ is an isomorphism. Then the canonical map $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map] is an isomorphism, and for every algebraic space $T\to Y$ the canonical map $f_T^\sharp:\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X\times_YT}$ is an isomorphism, where $f_T:X\times_YT\to T$ is the projection. Structure sheaves and direct images are on the small etale ringed sites with the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; $\Gamma$ denotes global sections of the structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0E6B, lemma-proper-flat-h0, hypothesis (2) for every field-valued morphism and conclusion (a)

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary algebraic space $T\to Y$; the choice $T=Y$ includes the first assertion. For every etale scheme chart $v:U\to T$, put $Z=X\times_YU$ and $p:Z\to U$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $p$ is proper, flat and finitely presented. For every field-valued $w:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$, associativity of the sheaf fibre product identifies $Z_w$ with $X_{vw}$, including the projections to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so its scalar map is the assumed isomorphism. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], restriction of $(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X\times_YT}$ to $U$ is $p_*\mathcal O_Z$. This identifies the restricted structure map with $p^\sharp$: their projections to every etale chart $(W,a)$ are both $s\mapsto a^\sharp(s)$ by [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map]. It remains to prove $p^\sharp$ invertible for each such scheme $U$.

source.place: Tag 0E6B, first sentence and last sentence of proof (a); Tags 03MO, 03XR, 04WP and 03LX

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] to $p$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Z$. This coefficient is quasi-coherent and finitely presented, with its identity rank-one presentation, and is flat over $U$ precisely by flatness of $p$. Write $A=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_Z$, $K=R\epsilon_{U,*}A$, and $a:\mathcal O_U[0]\to K$ for the derived scalar unit. The cited statement gives that $K$ is perfect, an isomorphism $\epsilon_U^*K\to A$ given by the canonical counit, and arbitrary scheme base change for $K$ preserving $a$. A perfect complex has quasi-coherent cohomology, so $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)$.

source.place: Tag 0E6B, perfectness and arbitrary base change from Tag 0CTM; Tag 0E62, first paragraph

proof.text: Record the degree-zero normalization, also for every base change of $p$ to a scheme $V$. The small ringed sites have enough injectives and K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]: its monomorphism from $M[0]$ into a degreewise injective complex gives an embedding of each module $M$ into its degree-zero injective term. The direct image $p_{V,*}$ is additive and left exact, being the right adjoint of tensor pullback in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. By [lem-sbc-right-derived-single-zero-unit], the canonical augmentation $(p_{V,*}\mathcal O)[0]\to Rp_{V,*}\mathcal O$ induces the standard isomorphism $p_{V,*}\mathcal O\simeq H^0(Rp_{V,*}\mathcal O)$. The derived scalar unit is the single complex of $p_V^\sharp$ followed by this augmentation. The canonical counit $\epsilon_V^*K_V\to Rp_{V,*}\mathcal O$ takes $\epsilon_V^*a_V$ to that unit: this is the counit triangle identity for the composite scalar adjunction. Exactness of $\epsilon_V^*$ in [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] therefore identifies $\epsilon_V^*H^0(a_V)$ with the actual map $p_V^\sharp$, not merely with some isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0E6B, canonical structure map; Tags 0156, 070K, 08H8 and 071Q; degree-zero augmentation normalization

proof.text: For a point $u\in U$ let $i_u:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$. By [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change], $Li_u^*(K,a)$ is $(K_{p_u}(\mathcal O),a_{p_u})$. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $\mathcal O_{Z_u}\to I^\bullet$ using [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]. By [lem-sp-kinjective-computes], it is K-injective and computes the unbounded direct image as $p_{u,*}I^\bullet$. This complex has zero terms below zero, hence zero negative cohomology. The counit identifies it with $\epsilon_{\kappa(u)}^*Li_u^*K$. Since this pullback is exact and faithful by [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], $H^j(Li_u^*K)=0$ for $j<0$. The small ringed-site hypotheses and enough injectives are those established in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0E62, first paragraph (nonnegative derived fibres); derived.tex Tags 013K, 05TD and 05TH

proof.text: By Step 3 on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$, the etale pullback of $H^0(Li_u^*a)$ identifies with $p_u^\sharp$. Both sides are quasi-coherent: the target is $H^0$ of the exact etale pullback of the perfect object $Li_u^*K$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Its inverse is restriction to Zariski opens, with comparisons the identity on open sections. Thus $H^0(Li_u^*a)$, evaluated on the unique nonempty Zariski open of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$, is exactly $\kappa(u)\to\Gamma(Z_u,\mathcal O_{Z_u})$. The definition [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] computes the right side as compatible functions on etale charts, and [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map] computes the arrow by scalar pullback. It is an isomorphism by Step 1. A map of modules on this one-point Zariski space is an isomorphism when its value there is bijective; hence $H^0(Li_u^*a)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E62, residue-field scalar isomorphism; descent.tex Tags 03DX and 03FH, normalized restriction inverse

proof.text: The scheme $U$, the perfect object $K$ and the morphism $a$ now satisfy [lem-sc-perfect-degree-zero-fibre-criterion]: Step 4 gives all negative-fibre vanishings and Step 5 gives the scalar isomorphism at every residue field. That statement yields $H^0(a):\mathcal O_U\to H^0(K)$ invertible. Exact etale pullback preserves its inverse. By the normalized comparison of Step 3, this is precisely invertibility of $p^\sharp:\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}\to p_*\mathcal O_Z$.

source.place: Tag 0E62, perfect-complex fibre criterion applied after Tag 0CTM

proof.text: By Step 1, $f_T^\sharp$ is an isomorphism on every etale scheme chart of $T$. These charts cover its small etale site. The local inverses agree on overlaps, since two inverses to the same map agree; the sheaf gluing axiom therefore glues them to an inverse to $f_T^\sharp$. This works for the arbitrary $T\to Y$ fixed in Step 1, including $T=Y$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E6B (lemma-proper-flat-h0), etale reduction and cohomology/base change; the existing perfect-complex criterion of Tag 0E62 (perfect.tex, lemma-proper-flat-h0) supplies the scheme-base linear-algebra step instead of reintroducing its rank-locus machinery.
